docs.title: Deliverance platform manual
docs.text:
Welcome to the manual of Deliverance Platform, the platform that brings the management of an organization's robots and IoT devices together in a single panel, whatever the manufacturer of each device.

This manual covers Platform 0.9.2 and API 0.11.2 (November 2026). The changes since the previous edition are in What's new.

This manual has three parts:

  • Introduction

    What the platform is, the basic concepts worth knowing and how to get started.

    Start here

  • User guide

    How to use each screen of the platform from the browser: Dashboard, Devices, Monitor, Operation, Workflows, Analytics, User Settings and Admin.

    Go to the guide

  • API reference

    Documentation of the REST API for integrating by code: authentication, available endpoints and explanation of the fields.

    Go to the reference

docs.title: Where do I start?
docs.text:
If you are... Start with A user who will work with the platform day to day Getting started, then the User guide An administrator setting up robots and automations Operation and Workflows A developer who wants to integrate by code API reference and Authentication

The screenshots show fictitious organizations, users and devices.

docs.title: Admin: Admin panel
docs.text: Management of users and organizations. It only appears to administrators, who manage their own organization and those below it.

docs.title: Users
docs.text: List of users: name, email, organization, role and status. The menu in each row lets you edit or delete the user.

docs.title: Add a user
docs.text:
• Email and Full name.
  • Organization: the organization the user belongs to.
  • Password and Confirm Password: initial password.
  • Superuser: administrator of their organization and those below it.
  • Active: if unchecked, the user cannot log in.

docs.title: Organizations
docs.text: The organizations by hierarchy, with their level and tier. Your own is marked as Current and its actions are disabled.

docs.title: Add an organization
docs.text: Name, description, address and Parent Organization, the organization it sits under.

docs.title: Organization tier
docs.text:
Tier details shows the contracted level (Watch, Operate or Orchestrate), the end of the contract, since when the organization has been in that level, the robots in service, who is billed, the contract reference and what it includes. The tier is changed by Deliverance.

Billed to shows who receives the bill. The administrator of the parent organization can include a child organization's bill in their own with Add its bill to...

Statuses: Active, Ends soon, Expired and Suspended. The end of a contract does not change anything by itself. When Deliverance suspends an organization, its users cannot enter the platform; its data, connectors and workflows continue.

docs.title: Analytics: Operation statistics
docs.text: Detailed report on the operations of the selected organization.

docs.title: Period and reports
docs.text:
• Daily, Weekly, Monthly or Custom (a date range). The report loads by itself; Generate Report reloads it.
  • Export PDF opens the browser's print dialog to save it.
  • Auto-email turns on periodic email delivery at the frequency of the selected period. It changes both the organization's setting and the user's; each user controls whether they receive it in User Settings.

docs.title: Robot Operations
docs.text: Tasks executed, success rate, failed tasks, average duration, tasks over time and performance per robot.

docs.title: IoT Operations
docs.text: Number of devices and how many have sent data, readings collected, energy consumed, and performance per meter and per sensor.

docs.title: Events
docs.text: The latest events of the period. Clicking a device opens it in Monitor. Full table opens the complete list, with filters by device and by type, and Export CSV:

docs.title: Dashboard: Control panel
docs.text: Control panel for the operations of the selected organization and those below it.

docs.title: Panel elements
docs.text:
1. Selection of the organization you are working on.
  2. Side navigation bar.
  3. Metric Stats: robot indicators since yesterday (see below).
  4. Welcome: greeting and the organization being viewed.
  5. Connected Devices: count by Robot, IoT and Sensor. The icon opens the list. A device counts as connected when it is running, idle or charging.
  6. Device Status: devices by status.
  7. Task List: latest robot tasks. Clicking one opens its detail.
  8. Task Status: tasks of the last 30 days by status.
  9. Filters (funnel icon) and Customize.

Further down are Device List (clicking a device opens its detail), Tasks History and Energy Consumption, the last two with a daily, weekly or monthly period.

docs.title: Metrics
docs.text:
Metric What it measures Task completion Mean completion of finished tasks. Cancelled tasks do not count; failed and expired tasks count as 0. Utilization Time working over time available and not charging. Availability Time in which the robot is not offline, in fault or stopped, over total time.

Green from 75% and yellow from 50%. A robot that has been offline for 7 days is considered out of service and does not count.

docs.title: Status Overview
docs.text: Expands the number of devices or tasks in each status:

docs.title: Filters
docs.text: They let you show only some organizations and device types. They are saved per user.

docs.title: Customize the panel
docs.text:
Customize lets you move the cards, change their width (¼, ½, ¾ or full), remove them and add others. The changes apply to all users of the organization when you click Save. An administrator can do it, or a user on their own organization. If someone else has saved first, you can choose which version to keep.

Cards that can be added:

  • Recent Activity: the latest alarms, battery warnings and task events.
  • Robot Status Timeline: what each robot has done in 24 hours or 7 days.
  • Start Tasks: start robot tasks (only administrators see it).
  • Camera View: the picture from a camera.

docs.title: Devices: Device management
docs.text:
Enable and manage devices across organizations.

Each row shows image, name, model, description, serial number, MAC address and ID. The row menu lets you edit or disable the device.

docs.title: Enable a device
docs.text: + Add Device opens the list of devices that belong to the organization but are disabled. Once enabled (Enable, or Enable All Devices for all of them) they appear in Dashboard, Monitor and Analytics.

docs.title: Assign a device to another organization
docs.text: Switch Organization (administrators only) transfers a device to your own organization or one of its children: choose the destination in Select Target and confirm with Transfer. Transferring a hub also transfers its meters.

docs.title: Filter the list
docs.text: Filter narrows the list by Name, Model, Serial Number, MAC Address, Description or ID.

docs.title: Device detail
docs.text: Selecting a row expands its details, with the Edit and Delete actions. A device that already has data cannot be deleted: it has to be disabled.

docs.title: Hubs and energy meters
docs.text: A hub's details list its meters (Individual Meters), which can be edited and enabled separately or all at once. Disabling a hub disables its meters.

docs.title: Edit a device
docs.text: You can change the name and description. For meters, also the wiring (Wiring: monophase or three-phase) and the name of each channel (Channel names).

docs.title: Login
docs.text: Identification and access to the platform.

docs.title: Log in
docs.text:
1. Enter your email and password in the form.
  2. Click Log In.

You can create an account from Sign up. An administrator then has to assign it to an organization before it shows any data.

docs.title: Recover your password
docs.text: Forgot password? asks for your email and sends a link to set a new password.

docs.title: Expired password and suspended organization
docs.text:
• Passwords are 8 to 40 characters long and expire 180 days after being changed. If yours has expired, the login asks for the current one and a new one (Update password).
  • Your organization is suspended. Contact Deliverance. means that the organization is suspended and none of its users can enter.

docs.title: Monitor: Device operation
docs.text: Monitors the operating data of the enabled devices of the selected organization. The left panel lists them and, when you select one, its detail is shown. At the top you choose between Simple and Advanced mode.

docs.title: Operation detail
docs.text: The content changes with the type of device.

docs.title: Delivery robot
docs.text: Status, battery, scene, last connection, current task, error code, Maintenance health (what is left before the next maintenance), task history and activity.

docs.title: Cleaning robot
docs.text: Adds the water levels (fresh and sewage) and the consumables (mop, filters, brushes...), each with its percentage.

docs.title: Sensor
docs.text: Measured magnitudes, date of the last reading and charts per magnitude (Temperature, Humidity, Light, Motion) with a period selector. A temperature-only sensor shows only that chart.

docs.title: Energy meter
docs.text: Current consumption, average and peak of the last 24 hours, and the Energy Consumption chart. A hub shows its meters; clicking one opens it.

docs.title: Camera
docs.text: Last alarm, last connection and Live Image: still pictures refreshed every few seconds, not video. If the latest is more than 30 seconds old, Not live is shown. Messages tell you if the camera is offline or has not sent a picture.

docs.title: Robot scene and map
docs.text:
The Scene card shows the robot on its map, with the building and floor; the expand button opens the whole map. The label shows how reliable the position is:

Label Meaning Exact Scale given by the manufacturer. Calibrated Calibrated by a user; the error is shown. Estimated Calculated from known points of the map. Rough Approximate position. Not calibrated The map is shown, without the robot's position.

docs.title: Status history
docs.text: The Status history strip summarizes the last 24 hours. Details (or the device's status label) opens the history of 24 hours, 7 or 30 days, with the time in each status, the battery and the changes.

docs.title: Activity
docs.text: Activity shows the latest things that have happened to the device. Full log opens the log with filters: Tasks, Connectors, Alarms, Signals and Status. View task opens the corresponding task.

docs.title: Alarms
docs.text:
Sensors and meters have a Configured Alarms block, where each alarm can be enabled, edited or deleted. Add alarm creates one:

  • Name: descriptive name (optional).
  • Magnitude: which value is watched.
  • Operator and Threshold value: the condition that triggers it. Present and Absent do not use a threshold.
  • Start date and End date (optional): period in which it applies.
  • Enabled: turn it off without deleting it.

When it goes off, it is recorded in the activity and the users of the organization with Alarm Notifications turned on are notified by email.

docs.title: Robot tasks
docs.text: Detailed Task List lists the tasks with date, type, status and name. Download lets you print the report or save it as PDF. Clicking a task expands its report, whose content depends on the robot:

docs.title: Advanced mode
docs.text: Advanced compares the readings of several meters and sensors in one chart: choose the range, the resolution, the magnitudes (Fields) and the devices, and click Generate. Split meter phases separates L1, L2 and L3.

docs.title: Operation: Robot operation
docs.text: Gives tasks to robots and shows what they are doing. It only appears to administrators. It has three views: Robot operation, Workflow operation (see Workflows) and Timeline.

docs.title: Robot operation
docs.text:
Choose the robot at the top. Below it are the current task, the scene, the battery and the error code, and three panels: Start a task, Running/Scheduled and Latest tasks. The Workflow label marks tasks launched by a workflow.

All brings all the robots together:

docs.title: Start a task
docs.text:
The list contains the tasks configured on the robot or, if the robot does not report them, those it has run in the last 90 days. Start starts the task and, if the robot is busy, Add to queue leaves it waiting. Confirmation is always requested.

A real robot may move

Once you confirm, the robot will start as soon as it can. Check first that the area is clear.

A scheduled task that does not start shows why it is waiting: the robot is busy, offline, in an emergency, in fault, paused or charging. If its deadline passes without it running, it is marked Not executed.

docs.title: Stop or cancel
docs.text:
• Stop (running task): the robot is asked to stop. The task stays running, marked Stop requested, until the robot confirms it.
  • Cancel (scheduled task): the robot will not run it.

This is not an emergency stop

Stop may take time, and not all robots or connectors support it. If the robot has to stop right now, it must be stopped on site.

docs.title: Connector errors
docs.text:
If the robot's connector does not carry out what was requested, a Connector error notice appears with the name of the task:

  • ...was not stopped: the connector has not stopped the task and the robot may still be moving. You can retry with Try again.
  • ...has not been taken: the connector has not taken the task. It may not be running or not be ready to start tasks, or the robot rejects it.

docs.title: Timeline
docs.text: Shows, by day or week, the tasks of each robot and the workflow runs, as a chart and as a table. The drop-down shows everything, only tasks or only workflows. If you are viewing another organization, only tasks are shown: workflows are those of your own.

docs.title: User Settings: User information
docs.text: Profile preferences and user settings.

docs.title: My profile
docs.text: The user's full name, email and picture, all editable.

docs.title: Organization
docs.text: ID, name, tier, description and address of the organization. Its logo can be changed here (JPEG, PNG or GIF, 5 MB maximum).

docs.title: Password
docs.text: Asks for the current password and the new one twice (8 to 40 characters).

docs.title: Appearance
docs.text: Interface theme: Light Mode or Dark Mode.

docs.title: Language
docs.text: English, Español or ​简体中文​. The choice is saved with the user's account.

docs.title: Reports & Alarms
docs.text:
• Analytics Reports: periodic emails with the analytics reports.
  • Alarm Notifications: email notice when an alarm goes off.

Alarms are configured per device in Monitor; here you decide whether this user receives the notice.

docs.title: Danger zone
docs.text: Deletes the account, with the user's personal data and settings. This action is permanent. It does not appear to administrators.

docs.title: Workflows: Automations
docs.text:
A workflow gives tasks to robots when something happens. It is managed in Operation → Workflow operation (administrators) and always belongs to your own organization, even if you are viewing another one.

  • Workflow collection: the workflows, with New workflow, an Active switch and a menu to open, duplicate or delete. A workflow has to be deactivated before it can be deleted.
  • Running/Scheduled: what is running and the next starts by time. A run can be paused, resumed or cancelled.
  • History: the latest runs.

On pause, the robot finishes the task it is running. On cancel, it is asked to stop it. A workflow with runs in progress cannot be deactivated.

docs.title: Editor
docs.text: Boxes are added from the palette (by clicking or dragging) and joined with arrows. Delete or Backspace removes what is selected. The Checks panel shows the problems. A workflow can only be activated if it is saved and has no problems, and while active it is read-only.

docs.title: Event
docs.text:
What starts the workflow: Kind of event and, optionally, which device sends it (Sent by).

Source Events Schedule A time arrives, on the chosen days (none = every day) Signals Pushbutton, spill detected, warehouse order, camera alert Tasks Starts, ends well, fails, is cancelled, expires, launched by hand Robot Offline, fault, emergency stop, starts charging, recovers, low battery Alarms An alarm goes off or clears

docs.title: Condition
docs.text:
Decides by Yes or No:

  • What the event carries: compares a value of the event.
  • How the task ended: whether it ended well, failed or was cancelled. Only right after a task.
  • Whether the robot has more tasks.

docs.title: Task
docs.text:
• Robot: the event's, the previous task's, a specific one or any of a model (the first one that is free, or the free one with most battery).
  • Task: the name of the task as it is on the robot. Empty: the event's value.
  • Deadline: minutes to start before expiring (0 = no deadline).
  • Retries: retries if it fails, and the wait between them.

docs.title: Rules
docs.text:
• Nothing can go into an event box.
  • Only a condition can follow a task.
  • There can be no cycles.

docs.title: What's new
docs.text: Edition for Platform 0.9.2 and API 0.11.2 (24 November 2026).

docs.title: In the platform
docs.text:
• Operation: new section for administrators. Start, stop and cancel robot tasks, with a timeline of what has run.
  • Workflows: visual automation editor with three boxes (event, condition and task), checks and run history.
  • Dashboard configurable per organization, with filters and new cards: Recent Activity, Camera View, Robot Status Timeline and Start Tasks.
  • Monitor: cameras, status history, device activity, robot position on its map and an advanced chart mode.
  • Analytics: events tab with CSV export.
  • Metrics: Compliance is now called Task completion, and Utilization and Availability are now calculated over time.
  • Connector errors made visible: if a connector does not start or stop a task, the platform says so.
  • Tiers of organizations, and suspension.
  • Languages: English, Español and ​简体中文​.

docs.title: In the API
docs.text:
• New groups: workflows, events, kpis, robot-maps, settings and subscriptions.
  • devices and tasks: task catalog, start, cancellation, timeline, camera image and meter configuration.
  • Superuser scope: only their own organization and those below it.
  • Only one task can be running per robot (409), and a device with data cannot be deleted, only disabled (409).
  • GET /switch-database/{data_source} is removed.

docs.title: Accessing the platform
docs.text:
Users sign in from the login page with their email and password. The Sign up link lets you create an account, but it shows no data until an administrator assigns it to an organization.

More details in Login.

docs.title: General navigation
docs.text:
Once inside, every screen of the platform is laid out the same way:

  • Left side menu: access to the main sections. Operation and Admin only appear to administrators.
  • Organization selector, at the top of the side menu: your own organization and, below it, its child organizations. It changes the data you see, not the organization you belong to. When you log in you always start in your own.
  • User menu, top right: My profile and Log out.
  • Version, at the bottom of the side menu: the deployed versions of the platform and the API.

The Dashboard also includes the data of the child organizations; Devices, Monitor and Analytics show only the selected organization.

docs.title: Quick map of sections
docs.text: Section What it is for Dashboard Configurable control panel with indicators, devices and tasks. Devices Enabling, editing and assigning devices between organizations. Monitor Real-time operating status of each device. Operation Giving tasks to robots, workflows and timeline (administrators). Analytics Operation and event reports, exportable. User Settings Profile, password, appearance, language and notifications. Admin Users, organizations and tiers (administrators).

docs.title: What is Deliverance Platform?
docs.text:
Deliverance Platform brings the management of an organization's robotic and IoT devices (robots, sensors, cameras and meters) together in a single panel, whatever the manufacturer of each device.

From the platform you can enable and organize devices, monitor their operation in real time, give tasks to robots, automate them with workflows, view usage and consumption analytics, and manage users and organizations.

docs.title: Key concepts
docs.text:
Before reading the rest of the manual, it helps to be clear on these concepts, which appear on almost every page:

  • Organization: the entity (customer, site, department) that devices and users belong to. The platform supports several organizations and a hierarchy between them (levels).
  • Administrator: a user marked as Superuser. Manages their own organization and those below it, never any others.
  • Tier: the level an organization has contracted: Watch, Operate or Orchestrate.
  • Device: any robot, IoT element or sensor registered in the platform. Devices fall into three categories: Robot, IoT and Sensor (cameras are sensors).
  • Connector: the component that links the platform to a manufacturer's devices. If a failure comes from the connector, the platform shows it as Connector error.
  • Task: an operation run by a robot (cleaning, delivery, etc.), with its own status, history and metrics.
  • Workflow: an automation: when an event occurs, and if certain conditions are met, a robot receives a task.
  • Event: something that has happened and is recorded: a task that ends, a robot that goes offline, an alarm, etc.
  • Scene: the location (building and floor) where a device operates. A robot can be shown on its map.

docs.title: How this manual is organized
docs.text:
• User guide: explains each screen of the platform from the point of view of someone using it in the browser.
  • API reference: documents the REST endpoints available to anyone who wants to integrate with Deliverance by code.

docs.title: API Reference: Introduction and authentication
docs.text: The Deliverance Platform API is a REST API (OpenAPI 3.1), mounted under the prefix /api/v1. The full OpenAPI schema is available at /api/v1/openapi.json, and can be explored interactively in the backend's own Swagger UI.

docs.title: Authentication
docs.text:
Most endpoints require authentication (Swagger marks them with the padlock icon 🔒). The flow is:

  1. Get a token by calling POST /api/v1/login/access-token with the user's credentials.
  2. Send that token as a Bearer token in the Authorization header of all other requests.

Endpoints without a padlock (for example POST /api/v1/users/signup or GET /api/v1/utils/health-check/) are public and need no token.

See the details of these endpoints in login.

docs.title: Open the interactive documentation (Swagger UI)
docs.text: The backend itself serves interactive API documentation at <host>/docs, generated automatically from the OpenAPI schema (for example, if the API is deployed at https://api.example.com, the interactive documentation is at https://api.example.com/docs). There you can see each endpoint and its input and output format, and try it directly from the browser without writing any request by hand: press the Authorize button at the top right, paste the access token (see below how to get it), and from then on any endpoint can be run from the page itself with the Try it out button.

docs.title: Try the API from the terminal
docs.text:
To use the API outside the browser, with curl or any other HTTP client, the full flow has two steps: request a token, and use it in the next request.

# 1. Get the token with the user's credentials
TOKEN=$(curl -s -X POST 'https://<host>/api/v1/login/access-token' \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/x-www-form-urlencoded' \
  -d 'grant_type=password&username=user@example.com&password=myPassword' \
  | python3 -c 'import sys, json; print(json.load(sys.stdin)["access_token"])')

# 2. Use that token on any protected endpoint, in the Authorization header
curl -s 'https://<host>/api/v1/devices/' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN"

The first command saves the token in the TOKEN variable (extracting it from the JSON response with Python), and the second reuses it to request the list of devices as an example. The same pattern works for any other endpoint in this reference: only the path and the method change (GET to read, POST to create, PUT/PATCH to modify, DELETE to delete).

docs.title: Conventions
docs.text:
• Resources with {id} / {uid} / {scene_id} / etc. in the path operate on a specific item.
  • Verbs follow the usual REST convention: GET (read), POST (create), PUT/PATCH (update), DELETE (delete).

docs.title: Token and password lifetime
docs.text: The token expires after 8 days (default value) and cannot be renewed: request a new one. The password expires 180 days after it was changed; once it has expired a token can still be obtained, but only PATCH /api/v1/users/me/password works.

docs.title: devices
docs.text:
Devices, their status, tasks, alarms and readings.

Method Path Who Description GET /api/v1/devices/ User Lists the devices. POST /api/v1/devices/ User Creates a device in the user's organization. GET /api/v1/devices/status User Status of all of them. GET /api/v1/devices/{uid}/status User Status of one. GET /api/v1/devices/{uid}/status/history User Status history (see kpis). GET /api/v1/devices/{uid}/snapshot User Image from a camera. GET /api/v1/devices/{id} User One device. PUT /api/v1/devices/{id} User Updates it. DELETE /api/v1/devices/{id} Superuser Deletes it. 409 if it already has data: it must be disabled instead. GET /api/v1/devices/own/{owner_id} User Those of an organization. GET /api/v1/devices/{uid}/tasks User Tasks of the device. POST /api/v1/devices/{uid}/tasks User Creates a task. 409 if one is already running. GET /api/v1/devices/{uid}/task-catalog Operator Tasks it can be given. GET /api/v1/devices/{uid}/operation Operator What it is doing: active, queue and recent. POST /api/v1/devices/{uid}/start-task Operator Starts a task by its name. GET /api/v1/devices/{uid}/alarms User Alarms. POST /api/v1/devices/{uid}/alarms User Creates an alarm. GET /api/v1/devices/{uid}/alarms/{alarm_id} User One alarm. PATCH /api/v1/devices/{uid}/alarms/{alarm_id} User Updates it. DELETE /api/v1/devices/{uid}/alarms/{alarm_id} User Deletes it. GET /api/v1/devices/{uid}/readings/{resolution} User Readings at that resolution. GET /api/v1/devices/{uid}/readings/{resolution}/{measure_type} User Readings of one measure. GET /api/v1/devices/{uid}/meter-config User Names of a meter's channels. PUT /api/v1/devices/{uid}/meter-config User Replaces them: {"channels": {"L1": "Kitchen"}}.

Who can call: see the introduction.

docs.title: Create a device
docs.text:
name, model, category, serial_number and mac_address are required. The owner is always the user's organization, and enabled is false by default.

{
  "name": "Cleaning robot 04",
  "model": "X100",
  "category": "robot",
  "serial_number": "SN-00313",
  "mac_address": "AA:BB:CC:00:11:23"
}

The response adds uid and owner_id.

docs.title: category
docs.text: category (API) Grouped in the Dashboard as robot Robot sensor (includes cameras) Sensor meter IoT hub IoT

docs.title: status
docs.text:
Value Meaning running Doing its job idle On and free charging Charging paused Stopped on purpose, can continue emergency Emergency stop error Fault offline No connection

The stored text may come in a different case or with a value specific to the manufacturer. battery_level is null on devices without a battery.

docs.title: Start a task
docs.text:
GET /devices/{uid}/task-catalog returns {"data": [{"name", "type"}], "count", "from_robot"}. from_robot is false if the robot does not report its tasks and the list is the ones it has run lately.

POST /devices/{uid}/start-task with {"name": "Table 4"} creates a Scheduled task. It responds 409 if it is not an enabled robot and 422 if the robot does not have that task (the name must match exactly).

Warning

A real robot may move.

docs.title: snapshot: image from a camera
docs.text: Returns image (data URL or null), taken_at, error and unchanged. Each call requests new images, so it must be repeated every few seconds; the first one may bring no image. With known_taken_at, an image you already have is not sent again. It responds 404 if it is not a camera.

docs.title: readings
docs.text:
limit_data_points (500 by default) limits the points. With no readings it responds 404. Usual values:

resolution Applies to 5min Meters and sensors 60min Meters and sensors 1day Meters and sensors Device type measure_type Unit Meter energy Wh Meter power W Meter voltage V Meter current A Meter power_factor (no unit) Meter reactive_power VAr Sensor temperature °C Sensor humidity % Sensor light lux Sensor motion (no unit)

docs.title: alarms
docs.text:
Field Meaning Values device_uid The device Required source Which data is watched status, error_code, battery_level, reading, maintenance, last_connection (minutes) operator How it is compared equals, lt, lte, gt, gte, present, absent value The threshold An object: {"threshold": 20} extra Parameters measure_type and endpoint_name for reading; key for maintenance start_date Since when Required

source and operator are not validated: an alarm with an unknown value never goes off.

{
  "device_uid": "11111111-1111-4111-8111-111111111111",
  "name": "Low battery",
  "source": "battery_level",
  "operator": "lt",
  "value": {"threshold": 20},
  "start_date": "2026-11-24T00:00:00"
}

When it goes off and when it clears, an alarm or alarm_cleared event is recorded (see events).

docs.title: events
docs.text:
Log of what happens. It is read-only: events cannot be created, modified or deleted through the API.

Method Path Who Description GET /api/v1/events/ User Lists the events, from newest to oldest. GET /api/v1/events/{uid} User One event.

Who can call: see the introduction.

Filters: organization_id (by default, one's own, not including those below it), event_type, device_uid, trigger_type (repeatable), since (inclusive), until (exclusive), skip and limit (1–1000). They apply to occurred_at.

Field Meaning occurred_at / created_at When it happened / when it was recorded category device, connector, workflow, activity (user actions) or system actor_type, actor_id, actor_name Who: user, integration or system subject_type, subject_id, subject_name About what; the name is the one at that moment event_type trigger for what happens to devices; other values for activity (create_user, workflow_enabled...)

docs.title: Event types
docs.text:
In a trigger event, description.trigger_type is:

Group Values Tasks task_started, task_completed, task_failed, task_cancelled, task_expired, task_manual Robot robot_offline, robot_fault, robot_emergency, robot_charging, robot_recovered (after 60 seconds in that state), battery Alarms alarm, alarm_cleared Signals button, spill, shipping_order, camera_alarm Connectors connector_error (payload: stop, not_taken or no_data), connector_recovered

description.late means it was recorded late; such an event does not start workflows.

{
  "data": [{
    "uid": "33333333-3333-4333-8333-333333333333",
    "event_type": "trigger",
    "priority": "info",
    "organization_id": "00000000-0000-4000-8000-000000000001",
    "description": {"trigger_type": "battery", "payload": "18", "device_uid": "11111111-1111-4111-8111-111111111111"},
    "occurred_at": "2026-11-24T10:00:00Z",
    "created_at": "2026-11-24T10:00:02Z",
    "category": "device",
    "actor_type": "system",
    "subject_type": "device",
    "subject_id": "11111111-1111-4111-8111-111111111111",
    "subject_name": "Robot 01"
  }],
  "count": 1
}

docs.title: API Reference: Introduction
docs.text: This reference covers API 0.11.2.

docs.title: What is a REST API?
docs.text: A REST API is a standard way for one program to talk to another over the internet: instead of opening the browser and clicking buttons, a program sends an HTTP request to a specific address (endpoint) and receives a response, usually in JSON format. Each endpoint has a method (GET to read, POST to create, PUT/PATCH to modify, DELETE to delete) and a path (for example /api/v1/devices/).

docs.title: What is the Deliverance API for?
docs.text: It gives access from code to what can be seen and done in the platform: devices, tasks, workflows, events, metrics, organizations and users. Use it to integrate the data into another system, automate actions or build your own tools.

docs.title: Categories (tags)
docs.text: Category Contents login Get and verify the access token. users Users. organizations Organizations, hierarchy, metrics and reports. devices Devices, status, tasks, alarms and IoT readings. tasks Robot tasks: query, cancellation and timeline. workflows Automations and their runs. events Event log (read-only). kpis Current indicators and status history. scenes Scenes (buildings) of an organization. robot-maps Floors, robot maps and their calibration. settings User and organization preferences. subscriptions Organization tiers. utils Service check.

docs.title: Who can call each endpoint
docs.text:
Label Meaning Public No token. User Any active user, on the data of their organization. A superuser also reaches the organizations below it. Superuser Superusers only, on their organization and those below it. Operator Whoever can operate robots and workflows; today, superusers.

A user with no organization has no access to any data.

docs.title: Basic fields and patterns
docs.text:
• Identifiers: they are UUIDs. The field is called uid in every resource except users, where it is id.
  • Dates and times: ISO 8601 format. Without a time zone, they are UTC.
  • Lists: they return an object {"data": [...], "count": 12}. In paginated lists, count is the total available; in non-paginated ones, the number of items returned.
  • Pagination: skip (how many to skip) and limit (the maximum number to return).
  • Free fields: category, type and status are text with no closed list. Compare them case-insensitively and tolerate unknown values.

docs.title: Common errors
docs.text: Code Meaning 400 Invalid request; some paths also use it for insufficient permissions. 401 / 403 No token, invalid or expired token, or no permission. 403 password_expired Expired password: only changing the password works. 403 organization_suspended The user's organization is suspended. 404 Does not exist. 409 Conflict with the current state (described on each page). 422 The data is not valid.

docs.title: kpis
docs.text:
Indicators for this moment and status history. For a period, see metric-stats in organizations.

Method Path Who Description GET /api/v1/organizations/{id}/kpis User Current indicators. GET /api/v1/devices/{uid}/status/history User Status changes since since (limit 1–5000, 500 by default). Kept for about 35 days.

Who can call: see the introduction.

{
  "t": "2026-11-24T10:00:00Z",
  "source": "stored",
  "accumulated_since": "2026-11-01T00:00:00Z",
  "robots": {"in_service": 3, "by_status": {"idle": 2, "charging": 1}},
  "availability": 100.0,
  "utilization": 0.0,
  "operative": 66.67,
  "compliance": null,
  "mtbf_hours": 120.5,
  "mttr_hours": 0.4
}
Field Meaning availability, utilization, operative Of the robots in service, at this moment compliance Today always null: it needs a planned time mtbf_hours Operating hours between faults, since accumulated_since mttr_hours Hours per repaired fault, since accumulated_since source stored (recorded recently) or live (calculated on request)

docs.title: login
docs.text:
Authentication and password recovery.

Method Path Who Description POST /api/v1/login/access-token Public Gets the token from the credentials. POST /api/v1/login/test-token User Checks the token and returns the user. POST /api/v1/password-recovery/{email} Public Sends the recovery email. POST /api/v1/reset-password/ Public Sets a new password: {"token", "new_password"}.

Who can call: see the introduction.

docs.title: Example
docs.text:
The request is sent as application/x-www-form-urlencoded, not as JSON:

curl -X POST 'https://<host>/api/v1/login/access-token' \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/x-www-form-urlencoded' \
  -d 'grant_type=password&username=user@example.com&password=myPassword'

{"access_token": "eyJhbGciOi...", "token_type": "bearer"}

That access_token is sent in all other requests, in the Authorization: Bearer <access_token> header.

docs.title: organizations
docs.text:
Organizations, their hierarchy, metrics and reports.

Method Path Who Description GET /api/v1/organizations/ User Lists the organizations within reach. POST /api/v1/organizations/ Superuser Creates an organization. GET /api/v1/organizations/{id} User One organization. PUT /api/v1/organizations/{id} User Updates it. Only a superuser changes the parent. DELETE /api/v1/organizations/{id} Superuser Deletes it. Never one's own. GET /api/v1/organizations/{id}/child User Direct children (one level). GET /api/v1/organizations/{id}/devices User Devices, with their status. GET /api/v1/organizations/{id}/scenes User Scenes. GET /api/v1/organizations/{id}/task-stats User Tasks since start_date (until end_date or now). GET /api/v1/organizations/{id}/metric-stats User Metrics for the period, with no breakdown. GET /api/v1/organizations/{id}/metrics User Metrics for the period, per device. POST /api/v1/organizations/{id}/send-report User Sends the PDF report to the caller's email. 503 if email is not configured. GET /api/v1/organizations/{id}/image User Logo. POST /api/v1/organizations/{id}/image User Uploads the logo (multipart, 10 MB maximum). DELETE /api/v1/organizations/{id}/image User Deletes the logo.

Who can call: see the introduction.

See also kpis, settings, robot-maps and subscriptions.

docs.title: metrics and metric-stats
docs.text:
Both require start_date and end_date (YYYY-MM-DD, days in UTC). metrics adds the per_device breakdown. Only robots count; one with no connection for 7 days is out of service.

Metric How it is calculated compliance_percentage Average completion of finished tasks (failed and expired count as 0; cancelled are left out). utilization_percentage Time working over time available and not charging. availability_percentage Time not disconnected, faulty or stopped, over the total. operative_percentage Time working or free, over the total.

Any of them can be null if there is no data. metric-stats also includes the tasks by result, total_devices, out_of_service_devices, period_start, period_end, updated_at and the addends (working_seconds, usable_seconds, available_seconds, operative_seconds, total_seconds, completion_sum).

To combine several organizations, add up the seconds; do not average the percentages. In metrics, cleaning_hours is the hours working, whatever the robot.

docs.title: Other fields
docs.text: Field Meaning parent_id Parent organization. In a root organization it points to itself. report_enabled Whether report emails are on. report_frequency List with daily, weekly and/or monthly.

docs.title: Hierarchy and permissions
docs.text: A superuser manages their organization and the whole branch below it. A regular user only sees their own.

docs.title: Example: create an organization
docs.text:
{
  "name": "North Site",
  "parent_id": "00000000-0000-4000-8000-000000000001",
  "report_enabled": true,
  "report_frequency": ["weekly"]
}

The response adds uid.

docs.title: robot-maps
docs.text:
Floors of each scene, robot maps and their calibration. Maps are created by the connectors; through the API they are placed, renamed, calibrated and deleted.

Method Path Who Description GET /api/v1/scenes/{scene_uid}/floors User Floors of a scene. POST /api/v1/scenes/{scene_uid}/floors User Creates a floor. 409 if the index already exists. PUT /api/v1/floors/{floor_uid} User Modifies it. DELETE /api/v1/floors/{floor_uid} User Deletes it. 409 if it has maps. GET /api/v1/organizations/{organization_id}/robot-maps User Maps, with their robots (no image). GET /api/v1/robot-maps/{map_uid} User One map. PUT /api/v1/robot-maps/{map_uid} User Renames it or places it on a floor. DELETE /api/v1/robot-maps/{map_uid} User Deletes it. 409 if there are robots on it. GET /api/v1/robot-maps/{map_uid}/image User PNG or JPEG image (with ETag). POST /api/v1/robot-maps/{map_uid}/calibration/preview User Tries a calibration without saving it. PUT /api/v1/robot-maps/{map_uid}/calibration User Saves the calibration (replaces the pairs). POST /api/v1/robot-maps/{map_uid}/calibration/live-pair User Pair with a robot's current position, without saving it.

Who can call: see the introduction.

calibration_level:

Value Meaning exact Manufacturer's scale calibrated Two or more pairs from a user estimated Two or more pairs from the connector rough A single pair and an assumed scale none Not calibrated: the position is not drawn

world_to_pixel is [[a, b, tx], [c, d, ty]]: u = a·x + b·y + tx, v = c·x + d·y + ty, from meters to pixels (v downwards). heading is in radians, counterclockwise from +x. For floors, index 0 is the ground floor and negative values are basements.

docs.title: Example: calibrate
docs.text:
{
  "points": [
    {"pixel": [10, 20], "world": [0, 0]},
    {"pixel": [210, 20], "world": [10, 0]}
  ],
  "use_manual_on_exact": false
}

Up to 50 pairs are accepted. The response contains world_to_pixel, calibration_level, calibration_error_m, resolution_m_per_px, rotation_deg and points. live-pair responds 422 if the robot is not on the map or its position is more than 120 seconds old.

docs.title: scenes
docs.text:
Scenes: the buildings where the devices operate. Their floors and maps are in robot-maps.

Method Path Who Description GET /api/v1/scenes/ User Lists the scenes within reach. POST /api/v1/scenes/ User Creates a scene. GET /api/v1/scenes/{scene_id} User One scene. PUT /api/v1/scenes/{scene_id} User Updates it. DELETE /api/v1/scenes/{scene_id} User Deletes it.

Who can call: see the introduction.

docs.title: floorplan and items: free objects, this is their actual shape
docs.text:
The schema only says "object", with no more detail. The actual shape is a 3D plan with corners, walls and textures:

{
  "floorplan": {
    "corners": {
      "corner1": {"x": 0, "y": 0},
      "corner2": {"x": 400, "y": 0},
      "corner3": {"x": 400, "y": 300},
      "corner4": {"x": 0, "y": 300}
    },
    "walls": [
      {
        "corner1": "corner1",
        "corner2": "corner2",
        "frontTexture": {"url": "/plan3d/rooms/textures/wallmap.png", "stretch": true, "scale": 0},
        "backTexture": {"url": "/plan3d/rooms/textures/wallmap.png", "stretch": true, "scale": 0}
      }
    ],
    "wallTextures": [],
    "floorTextures": {},
    "newFloorTextures": {
      "corner1,corner2,corner3,corner4": {"url": "/plan3d/rooms/textures/hardwood.jpg", "scale": 100}
    }
  },
  "items": []
}

corners are named points; walls connects two corners to each other with its texture; items is a list of objects placed in the scene.

docs.title: Example: create a scene
docs.text:
Only organization_id is required:

{"label": "Main building", "organization_id": "00000000-0000-4000-8000-000000000001"}

The response adds uid, floorplan and items.

docs.title: settings
docs.text:
Preferences stored by key.

Method Path Who Description GET /api/v1/users/me/settings User All of one's own. GET /api/v1/users/me/settings/{key} User One. PUT /api/v1/users/me/settings/{key} User Saves it. DELETE /api/v1/users/me/settings/{key} User Deletes it. GET /api/v1/organizations/{id}/settings User Those of the organization. GET /api/v1/organizations/{id}/settings/{key} User One. PUT /api/v1/organizations/{id}/settings/{key} User Saves it, for all its users. DELETE /api/v1/organizations/{id}/settings/{key} User Deletes it.

Who can call: see the introduction.

Level Keys User ui.theme (light or dark), ui.language, dashboard.filters, dashboard.cardState Organization dashboard.layout

The value is any JSON up to 64 KB. version (optional) is the version the change starts from, 0 if it did not exist: if someone else saved first, it responds 409 with the current value. Without version the value is overwritten. When deleting, it goes in the query (?version=).

{"value": "dark", "version": 0}

docs.title: subscriptions
docs.text:
Tier of each organization.

Method Path Who Description GET /api/v1/subscriptions/tiers User The tiers and what they include. GET /api/v1/subscriptions User Tier of the organizations within reach (no trailing slash). GET /api/v1/organizations/{id}/subscription User Tier of an organization; the details, only for superusers. PUT /api/v1/organizations/{id}/subscription/payer Superuser Of the parent: whether its invoice includes the child's ({"billed_to_parent": true}). GET /api/v1/organizations/{id}/subscription/history Superuser Changes. GET /api/v1/organizations/{id}/subscription/usage Superuser Usage for a month (?month=YYYY-MM). GET /api/v1/organizations/{id}/subscription/robot-log Superuser Robots entering and leaving service.

Who can call: see the introduction.

tier is watch, operate or orchestrate. state is active, expiring (60 days or less), expired or suspended. The tier, the contract and the suspension are changed by Deliverance.

While an organization is suspended, its users receive 403 organization_suspended when logging in and on any call.

docs.title: tasks
docs.text:
Robot tasks.

Method Path Who Description GET /api/v1/tasks/ User Lists the tasks (summarized). POST /api/v1/tasks/ User Creates a task. 409 if the robot already has one running. GET /api/v1/tasks/{uid} User One task, with report and waypoints. POST /api/v1/tasks/{uid}/cancel Operator Cancels a waiting task or requests to stop a running one. 409 if it has already finished. GET /api/v1/tasks/timeline Operator Tasks of an organization between start and end (32 days maximum). GET /api/v1/tasks/operation Operator What the robots of an organization are doing: active, queue and recent.

Who can call: see the introduction.

To start a task configured on a robot, see start-task in devices. Tasks cannot be modified or deleted through the API.

docs.title: status and type
docs.text:
Situation status values Waiting Scheduled, Paused (by a paused workflow) Running Running, executing, or any other Finished Completed, Failed / error, Cancelled / canceled

Compare them case-insensitively. type is free text (for example Delivery or Cleaning).

docs.title: Cancel and stop
docs.text:
A waiting task becomes Cancelled immediately. With a running one, the robot is only requested to stop: stop_requested_at says when, and stop_failed becomes true if it has not been carried out 30 seconds later.

{"uid": "22222222-2222-4222-8222-222222222222", "status": "Running", "stop_requested_at": "2026-11-24T10:00:00"}

Danger

It is not an emergency stop.

docs.title: waiting_for
docs.text: Why a task whose time has come has not started: busy, offline, emergency, error, paused, charging (its robot) or connector (a problem with its connector, which has not picked it up).

docs.title: Lists do not include the full detail
docs.text: GET /tasks/ and GET /devices/{uid}/tasks do not include report or waypoints: request the individual task.

docs.title: report and waypoints
docs.text:
report has no fixed structure: each integration writes its own keys. Do not assume that a field always exists. waypoints is the path travelled, if the robot reports it.

{
  "uid": "22222222-2222-4222-8222-222222222222",
  "device_uid": "11111111-1111-4111-8111-111111111111",
  "task_name": "Ground floor cleaning",
  "type": "Cleaning",
  "status": "Completed",
  "start_time": "2026-11-18T09:00:00",
  "end_time": "2026-11-18T09:23:10",
  "report": {"duration": 1390, "distance": 245.3, "completed_percent": 98.4},
  "waypoints": [],
  "stop_requested_at": null,
  "stop_failed": false,
  "waiting_for": null
}

docs.title: users
docs.text:
Users: own profile and administration.

Method Path Who Description GET /api/v1/users/ Superuser Lists the users within reach. POST /api/v1/users/ Superuser Creates a user. 400 if the email already exists. GET /api/v1/users/me User The current user. PATCH /api/v1/users/me User Updates the current user. 409 if the email already exists. DELETE /api/v1/users/me User Deletes the current user (403 for superusers). PATCH /api/v1/users/me/password User Changes the password. POST /api/v1/users/signup Public Sign-up. The user is left with no organization. GET /api/v1/users/{user_id} User Oneself, or a user within reach. PATCH /api/v1/users/{user_id} Superuser Updates a user. DELETE /api/v1/users/{user_id} Superuser Deletes a user; never oneself. GET /api/v1/users/me/image User Own image. POST /api/v1/users/me/image User Uploads the image (multipart, field file, 10 MB maximum). DELETE /api/v1/users/me/image User Deletes the image. GET /api/v1/users/{user_id}/image User A user's image.

Who can call: see the introduction.

User preferences are in settings.

docs.title: Fields that are not self-explanatory
docs.text: Field Meaning is_active If false, the user cannot log in. is_superuser Administers their organization and those below it. report_enabled Receives the analytics reports by email. alarm_enabled Receives an email when an alarm goes off. organization_id Their organization, or null. Assigned by a superuser.

docs.title: Example: create a user
docs.text:
{
  "email": "new.user@example.com",
  "full_name": "New User",
  "password": "aSecurePassword123",
  "organization_id": "00000000-0000-4000-8000-000000000001",
  "is_superuser": false
}

The response adds id and the other fields, and never includes the password.

docs.title: utils
docs.text:
Method Path Who Description GET /api/v1/utils/health-check/ Public Checks that the service is up. Returns true.

Who can call: see the introduction.

docs.title: workflows
docs.text:
Automations and their runs. They always work on the user's organization: a superuser does not reach the workflows of the organizations below it. The concept is explained in the guide.

Method Path Who Description GET /api/v1/workflows/ User Lists the workflows. POST /api/v1/workflows/ Operator Creates one, disabled. GET /api/v1/workflows/{uid} User One workflow. PUT /api/v1/workflows/{uid} Operator Modifies it. 409 if it is enabled. DELETE /api/v1/workflows/{uid} Operator Deletes it. 409 if it is enabled. POST /api/v1/workflows/{uid}/enable Operator Enables it. 422 if it has problems. POST /api/v1/workflows/{uid}/disable Operator Disables it. 409 if it has live tasks. GET /api/v1/workflows/catalog Operator What can be used in a workflow. POST /api/v1/workflows/validate Operator Checks a diagram without saving it. GET /api/v1/workflows/runs Operator Runs in progress and next_starts. GET /api/v1/workflows/history Operator Finished runs (skip, limit up to 200). GET /api/v1/workflows/timeline Operator Runs between start and end (32 days maximum). POST /api/v1/workflows/runs/{run_id}/pause Operator Pauses. 409 if it is not in progress. POST /api/v1/workflows/runs/{run_id}/resume Operator Resumes. POST /api/v1/workflows/runs/{run_id}/cancel Operator Cancels.

Who can call: see the introduction.

Run states: running, scheduled, waiting, paused and cancelling. Results: completed, failed, cancelled and not_started.

docs.title: data: the diagram
docs.text:
It contains "version": 3, nodes (the boxes) and edges (the arrows).

{
  "name": "Delivery on request",
  "data": {
    "version": 3,
    "nodes": [
      {"id": "e1", "data": {"type": "event", "properties": {"triggerType": "button"}}},
      {"id": "t1", "data": {"type": "task", "properties": {"taskName": "Table 4", "robot": {"model": "T10"}}}}
    ],
    "edges": [{"source": "e1", "target": "t1"}]
  }
}
Box Properties event At least one of triggerType, userId or robot ({"uid"} or {"model"}). With schedule: hours (["07:30"]) and days (["mon"], empty = all). condition kind: event (field, operator, value), result (status: Completed, Failed or Cancelled; right after a task) or pending. task robot ({"uid"}, {"model"} or {"from": "event"} / {"from": "previous"}), rule (first_free or most_battery, only with a model), taskName, taskType, deadlineMinutes (30 by default, 0 = no deadline), retry (max 1–10, waitMinutes 0–1440).

On arrows leaving a condition, sourceHandle is yes or no. There can be no cycles and, after a task, only result conditions.

triggerType accepts schedule and the types in events. A type that does not exist gives no error: it never fires.

POST /workflows/validate responds {"runnable": true, "problems": []}; each problem carries code, message and box.
